name: Inspire art

subjectOf.text: Member States can avoid at least part of the result in Centros and Inspire Art by recharacterizing what used to be corporate law as creditor protection law, provided the recharacterized rule does not discriminate against foreign corporations.
subjectOf.abstract: this answer suggests that Member States can avoid at least part of the result in Centros and Inspire Art by recharacterizing what used to be corporate law as creditor protection law.
subjectOf.citation: Christian Kirchner, Richard W. Painter, Wulf A. Kaal, Regulatory Competition in EU Corporate Law after Inspire Art Unbundling Delaware's Product for Euro (2004). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=617681

subjectOf.text: Empirically, at least 48 companies with German names carrying the GmbH designation were formed as private limited companies under U.K. law in the ten months after the Inspire Art decision, indicating that charter migration accelerated after the ruling.
subjectOf.abstract: In the ten months after the Inspire Art decision, at least 48 such companies with German names and the designation GmbH in their names were formed as private limited companies under U.K. law.
subjectOf.citation: Christian Kirchner, Richard W. Painter, Wulf A. Kaal, Regulatory Competition in EU Corporate Law after Inspire Art Unbundling Delaware's Product for Euro (2004). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=617681
scope_conditions: some of these companies may also do business in the U.K. or be affiliated with a German GmbH
